findings.title: Sync DB call blocks event loop
findings.problem: project_admin_or_admin_or_maintainer_access is declared `async def` but calls `with get_session() as session: user_project_repository.is_admin(session, user.id, project_name)` — a synchronous, blocking DB session/query — for every request to the new project-scoped activity endpoint made by a non-admin/non-maintainer caller (i.e. a project admin, the endpoint's primary intended user).
findings.impact: Blocks the async event loop for the duration of the DB round-trip on every project-admin request, degrading concurrency/throughput across the whole FastAPI process under load.
findings.recommendation: Use an async session/async is_admin lookup, or offload the sync call via asyncio.to_thread/run_in_executor.

findings.title: Scheduler budget events drop known project_name
findings.problem: ActiveProjectBudgetRestoreService._restore_project (line ~99), InactiveProjectBudgetStopService.run (inactive_project_budget_stop_service.py ~58), and InactiveCostCenterBudgetStopService.run (inactive_cost_center_budget_stop_service.py ~64) each emit PROJECT_BUDGET_RESTORED/PROJECT_BUDGET_STOPPED with `project_name=None`, even though the enclosing loop already holds the resolved `project_name` variable (or resolves it explicitly via aget_project_names_by_cost_center_name for the cost-center case).
findings.impact: These project-specific budget lifecycle events will never surface in that project's new activity trail, defeating the feature's purpose for the one budget domain where automatic, non-human-triggered actions are common.
findings.recommendation: Pass `project_name=project_name` (the already-resolved loop variable) instead of `project_name=None` at all three sites.

findings.title: project_name dropped on non-amount budget updates
findings.problem: update_project_budget only resolves `_assignment` (the source of project_name) inside the `if amounts_changed or data.models is not None:` branch; when only other fields such as budget_duration change, `_assignment` stays None and the emitted PROJECT_BUDGET_UPDATED event carries `project_name=None`, even though the budget row is a known PROJECT-type budget belonging to a specific project.
findings.impact: Project budget-duration-only updates are silently excluded from that project's activity trail — the same missing-attribution defect the spec called out for scheduler sites, now present in a manually-triggered path too.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the assignment/project_name unconditionally (e.g. via project_budget_assignment_repository.get_active_by_budget_id) rather than only inside the amounts/models sync branch.

findings.title: Customer-config audit events miss actor snapshot
findings.problem: _audit() builds ActivityEventCreate with only actor_id=actor.id; it never sets project_name/actor_email/actor_display_name, even though the full `actor: User` object (with .email/.name) is already in scope at both call sites (settings update and reset).
findings.impact: CUSTOMER_CONFIG SETTING_UPDATED/SETTING_RESET events are the one domain left with a blank actor snapshot after this change, so their actor identity is lost once the acting user is deleted — the exact regression this feature exists to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Pass actor_email=actor.email, actor_display_name=actor.name into the ActivityEventCreate call in _audit (project_name=None is correct here, since these events are not project-scoped).

findings.title: Migration safety test never touches a real DB
findings.problem: The migration-safety test only replays the module's op.add_column/create_index calls against a mock recorder and asserts no alter_column/execute call occurs; it never creates pre-existing rows, runs upgrade() against a database, and asserts that domain/event_type/entity_id/actor_id/created_at survive unchanged — the exact verification the spec called out as needing to close this gap.
findings.impact: The stated guarantee ('migration must not alter any existing row's protected column values') is checked only indirectly (no forbidden op call observed), not by an end-to-end assertion against real row data, leaving residual risk undetected if a future edit to this migration wraps a mutation differently.
findings.recommendation: Add an integration test that runs the migration against a test DB seeded with pre-existing activity_events rows and asserts their domain/event_type/entity_id/actor_id/created_at values are bit-for-bit unchanged after upgrade().
